As I do after every quarter, let me share the snapshot of the overall digital advertising industry.

Some key takeaways from 3Q’26:

Digital advertising industry decelerated from 20.2% in 2Q’26 to 16.1% in 3Q’26. As mentioned in my last quarter’s snapshot, given the tough comp I expected both Q3 and Q4 to experience deceleration.

Meta’s incremental share jumped to 52.7%. Outside the ATT-distorted 2022 numbers, this is the first time in this snapshot that $META captured more than half of the incremental dollar. There is a bit of an asterisk here. $AMZN moved Prime Day into June this year, so its ad growth slowed from 26% in 2Q’26 to 11% in 3Q’26, which mechanically flatters everyone else’s incremental share. If I combine 2Q and 3Q, Meta’s incremental share was ~48%. That is still comfortably ahead of its ~35% current share, so the share gain story remains fully intact even after adjusting for the Prime Day timing.

$GOOGL Search’s incremental share dropped to 27.6%, the lowest since 2Q’23 (which was again distorted by ATT). Last quarter I wondered whether Search could hold ~30% incremental share or would drift toward the mid-20s. But we need to adjust for the Prime Day impact here as well. On a combined 2Q and 3Q basis, Search’s incremental share was just a tad bit below 30%. Let’s wait a couple more quarters to see if $GOOG Search can stay around this level or keep drifting downwards.

As a reminder, the actual digital advertising industry is larger than what my snapshot below shows, but this snapshot helps me gauge the broader digital advertising industry’s big picture. TikTok and Walmart advertising are notably missing here. Well, TikTok is a private company and Walmart doesn’t disclose their advertising revenue consistently.

The frustrating part about the stablecoin drain is that the fix already exists.

Since 2022 stablecoin supply has moved inversely with T-bill yields (-0.62 correlation on 90-day changes). Rates aren't the only driver, but when bills pay more, stablecoins lose out because holders earn nothing.

Tokenised money market funds hold the same T-bills, pay you the yield & live onchain. In principle that makes them a better product than a stablecoin, and better than a traditional money fund too, as they can settle and be posted as collateral 24/7.

In TradFi, money funds grow when rates are high or markets are stressed, as people park cash. Onchain, they should be the offset when stablecoins shrink, but at $17.1B they're only 6% of stablecoin supply. Many of the big ones are for wealthy investors only (BlackRock's needs $5M, JPMorgan's $1M), and even the retail ones need ID checks, approved wallets and business-day redemptions.

Fix that and I expect this becomes one of the biggest growth areas onchain.
